result.summary: FINAL RE-GATE PASS (rework 3/3). Independently re-verified all four items against real source, not the design's own citations: (1) Letflow.Api.Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 (authorization.ex:408-418) reduces via role_from_string/1 (:420-426), a 6-clause exhaustive match on the closed role() type with a catch-all `nil` for anything else, dropped silently by the reduce accumulator -- read directly, confirmed roles_from_strings(["VIEWER"]) == []. (2) Grepped every real call site of roles_from_strings/1 and of conn.assigns.auth_context.roles across lib/: exactly 3 code call sites feed an access decision (authorize.ex:105, routers/entities.ex:2104, routers/tasks.ex:258), all route through roles_from_strings/1 before evaluate_access/2, confirmed by reading each. One additional raw-role consumer found and independently investigated: lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex:92-95 checks `@platform_admin not in roles` directly against conn.assigns.auth_context.roles (a real PLATFORM_ADMIN-exemption grant decision, bypassing roles_from_strings/1) -- this is a true statement the design's own §2.3 text does not literally claim to rule out (it scopes its claim precisely to 'into evaluate_access/2 or any role_allows?/2 check', which TenantStatus does not call), and independently confirmed immaterial to this rework's specific fix: none of the 3 named tests' fixtures ever sets tenant.status to :inactive, so that branch never fires in any of them, and 'VIEWER' != 'PLATFORM_ADMIN' either way -- reported here as a non-blocking observation, not a design defect (it does not misdescribe anything §1-§2.2 changed, and post-fix it actually becomes live-consistent too, since conn.assigns.auth_context.roles itself becomes the live-queried list for OIDC users after §1 lands). (3) Read all 3 cited test files at the cited lines directly: auth_pipeline_test.exs:167, api_pipeline_integration_test.exs:130, req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs:1053 all currently assert `roles == ["VIEWER"]` exactly as the design states, and all other cited assertions in each test (refute conn.halted / tenant_id / persisted checks in file 1; conn.status==403 / tenant_id / user_id in file 2; conn.status==403 / tenant_id / body["detail"]/entries-absence in file 3) are confirmed unaffected by the proposed change -- the proposed `assert roles == []` / `assert conn.assigns.auth_context.roles == []` edits are correct and sufficient to make each test pass again without weakening any of those other assertions. Also confirmed test/support/token_verifier_double.ex:36 mints realm_access.roles: ["VIEWER"] as cited, and read all 3 tests' own tenant-seeding helpers (insert_tenant_for_realm!/insert_bpm_default_tenant!) directly -- none seeds any tenant_role or group_members row, confirming the live query and one-time sync both correctly resolve to [] for this fixture. (4) Spot-checked §2.2's identity.ex citations (insert_or_fetch_group_member/3 exists as a private helper backing add_group_member/3, matching §2.2.2 step 2) -- nothing in §§0-2.2 needs to change as a result of §2.3's addendum; the TenantStatus finding in (2) does not require any change to §1-§2.2's design, only the observation recorded above. Design is complete, unambiguous, and contains no implementation code -- signatures/specs only throughout §§1-9.

issues.description: lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex:92-95 reads conn.assigns.auth_context.roles directly (raw strings, checking membership of literal 'PLATFORM_ADMIN') for its tenant-inactive-403 PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption, bypassing roles_from_strings/1 -- a real access-decision call site the design's §2.3 does not enumerate. Immaterial to this rework's 3-test fix (verified: no test's fixture sets tenant.status: :inactive, and 'VIEWER' is not 'PLATFORM_ADMIN' under either the old or new role-list contents), and not a regression introduced by this design (conn.assigns.auth_context.roles itself becomes live-queried for OIDC users once §1 lands, so this plug's exemption check becomes live-consistent too, as a side effect). Flagging for SECURITY-REVIEWER's own pass, not a design-phase blocker.
